content: Pretomanid has been shown to increase the plasma levels or pharmacological effects of drugs that are substrates of OATP1B3, OAT3, BCRP, or P-gp transporters. This interaction necessitates careful monitoring and potential dose adjustments to mitigate the risk of drug-related adverse effects. Below are detailed interactions and recommendations for specific drugs: 1. Erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, stearate): Co-administration with pretomanid may increase erythromycin levels or effects. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 2. Famotidine: Pretomanid increases famotidine levels or effects. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 3. Fexofenadine: Pretomanid elevates fexofenadine levels or effects. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 4. Fluvastatin: Pretomanid increases fluvastatin levels or effects. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 5. Furosemide: Pretomanid raises furosemide levels or effects. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 6. Ganciclovir: Pretomanid increases ganciclovir levels or effects. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 7. Glecaprevir/Pibrentasvir: Pretomanid elevates levels or effects of this combination. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 8. Glyburide: Pretomanid increases glyburide levels or effects. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 9. Imatinib: Pretomanid raises imatinib levels or effects. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 10. Indomethacin: Pretomanid increases indomethacin levels or effects. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 11. Letermovir: Pretomanid elevates letermovir levels or effects. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 12. Levothyroxine: Pretomanid increases levothyroxine levels or effects. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 13. Methotrexate: Pretomanid raises methotrexate levels or effects. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 14. Olmesartan: Pretomanid increases olmesartan levels or effects. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 15. Oseltamivir: Pretomanid elevates oseltamivir levels or effects. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 16. Paclitaxel: Pretomanid increases paclitaxel levels or effects. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 17. Penicillin G (aqueous): Pretomanid raises penicillin G levels or effects. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 18. Pitavastatin: Pretomanid elevates pitavastatin levels or effects. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 19. Pravastatin: Pretomanid increases pravastatin levels or effects. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 20. Prazosin: Pretomanid raises prazosin levels or effects. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 21. Revefenacin: Pretomanid elevates revefenacin levels or effects. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 22. Rifampin: Pretomanid increases rifampin levels or effects. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 23. Rosuvastatin: Pretomanid raises rosuvastatin levels or effects. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 24. Sulbactam/Durlobactam: Pretomanid elevates levels or effects of this combination. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 25. Sulfamethoxazole: Pretomanid increases sulfamethoxazole levels or effects. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 26. Sulopenem: Pretomanid raises sulopenem levels by inhibiting OAT3-mediated metabolism. Monitor for adverse reactions such as diarrhea and nausea. 27. Telmisartan: Pretomanid increases telmisartan levels or effects. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 28. Valsartan: Pretomanid elevates valsartan levels or effects. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 29. Verapamil: Pretomanid raises verapamil levels or effects. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 30. Voxilaprevir: Pretomanid increases voxilaprevir levels or effects. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 31. Zidovudine: Pretomanid elevates zidovudine levels or effects. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Serious Interactions Requiring Alternative Therapy: 1. Acetaminophen: Co-administration with pretomanid increases hepatotoxicity risk. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 2. Allopurinol: Increases toxicity risk when combined with pretomanid. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 3. Amiodarone: Co-administration increases toxicity risk. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 4. Amobarbital: Reduces pretomanid levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 5. Amoxicillin: Increases toxicity risk when combined with pretomanid. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 6. Apalutamide: Reduces pretomanid levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 7. Armodafinil: Reduces pretomanid levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 8. Atorvastatin: Increases toxicity risk when combined with pretomanid. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 9. Auranofin: Increases toxicity risk when combined with pretomanid. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 10. Azathioprine: Increases toxicity risk when combined with pretomanid. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 11. Bexarotene: Reduces pretomanid levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 12. Bosentan: Reduces pretomanid levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 13. Brigatinib: Reduces pretomanid levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 14. Busulfan: Increases toxicity risk when combined with pretomanid. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 15. Butabarbital: Reduces pretomanid levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 16. Butalbital: Reduces pretomanid levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 17. Carbamazepine: Reduces pretomanid levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. General Recommendations: Pretomanid is associated with hepatotoxicity. Avoid alcohol, hepatotoxic agents, and herbal supplements during therapy. Pretomanid is a CYP3A4 substrate. Avoid co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers. Monitor closely for adverse effects and consider dosage adjustments for drugs that are substrates of OAT3, OATP1B3, BCRP, or P-gp transporters.
